wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/fix_nullable_typespec.py: """The catalogue could not say `?int`, so `stream_select()`'s "block forever" became "poll".

php's stub is `stream_select($r, $w, $e, ?int $seconds, ?int $microseconds = null)`. The catalogue
declared `$seconds` as plain `Int` with no default, because nullability had nowhere to live: the
only thing resembling it is `default: Some(DefaultSpec::Null)`, which says what an OMITTED argument
becomes, and `$seconds` is REQUIRED. So a written `null` was coerced to `0` — and for this function
those are opposite instructions:

    stream_select($r, $w, $e, null)     blocks forever — there is no timeout
